Açığa Satış İşlemi: The transaction in which an investor sells an asset not held in its portfolio, for various reasons chief among them the expectation of a price decline, and delivers the asset by buying it from the market when the delivery time arrives.
Ağ etkisi: The phenomenon of a product's value increasing as more people use it.
Aşırı zenginlik: Although there is no precise definition, the state of holding wealth a thousand times or more above the average in a given society.
Aşırı özgüven: An investor's overestimating its forecasting ability and the quality of its information; it manifests itself as excessive trading, insufficient diversification and high risk.
Banka paniği: Or a bank run: the desire of a large number of depositors to withdraw their deposits from a bank at the same time.
Banka parası: Payment instruments held and tracked as account records by the banking system.
Bankacılık sistemi: A network of institutions with a regular structure, consisting of the banks operating in a country.
Bankalararası Kart Merkezi - BKM: A payment system with legal personality, established in 1990 through the partnership of 13 public and private Turkish banks to provide the clearing and settlement of debit and credit cards. Through BKM, banks carry out the clearing and settlement of the credit card and debit card payments they make on one another's behalf. BKM operates on a netting basis, and the settlement of the debts arising from netting takes place through the accounts held at the Istanbul Branch of the CBRT.
Bankalararası Para Piyasası: The market operating within the CBRT where banks can carry out TL Deposit Purchase-Sale Transactions with one another and with the CBRT, and — with only the CBRT as counterparty — Late Liquidity Window and Intraday Limit Transactions.
Bankalararası TL Aktarım Sistemi: As a component of the EFT System owned and operated by the CBRT, the system that provides the real-time electronic settlement of the payments banks make among themselves and of the banking payments related to the correspondent services they provide to financial institutions abroad.
Bankaya koşma: Or a bank panic: the desire of a large number of depositors to withdraw their deposits from a bank at the same time.
Bankaya Özgü Döngüsel Sermaye Tamponu: Refers to the additional core capital amount that banks are expected to hold, in order to prevent equity from falling short of the regulations on capital adequacy in the event that credit expansion reaches levels that can raise the general risk level of the financial sector.
Banknot: Bearing instruments that carry no interest, for which the issuing institution guarantees payment of the amount written on them to the bearer. They are legal tender. The CBRT is the only institution authorized to print Turkish lira banknotes.
Bant içinde sürünen kur: An exchange rate regime in which exchange rates are allowed to move within a certain band around a central parity, and the central parity itself is changed from time to time.
Barriers to Expansion: Expansion barriers are the obstacles preventing undertakings already present in the market from increasing their market shares.
Basel Bankacılık Denetim Komitesi: An international organization operating under the umbrella of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) based in Basel, Switzerland, which prepares prudential regulatory frameworks for the banking sector on a global scale. The Committee also provides cooperation on the supervision of banks. With the aim of consolidating global financial stability, the Committee issues regulatory frameworks, particularly in the fields of capital and liquidity, and monitors the implementation of these regulations in countries. The Committee submits its fundamental decisions and work programme to the Group of Central Bank Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS) for approval.
Basit para çarpanı: The money multiplier in the case where banks hold no free reserves and the non-bank sector uses no cash.
Baskın strateji: In game theory, the strategy that yields a player the highest payoff regardless of the other players' strategies.
Batmasına İzin Verilemeyecek Kadar Büyük: Financial institutions that carry the potential of creating systemic risk and can impose large costs on the economy should they become unable to continue their operations, owing to their size and complexity, their connections with other institutions in the financial system, and the difficulty for other financial institutions to provide their significant activities at short notice.
Baz Etkisi: Refers to the effect carried over to the period in which the change is calculated, when the reference period for the change contains a realization significantly lower or higher than normal. For example, in calculating the annual inflation rate for November 2014, the percentage change of the November 2014 consumer index relative to the November 2013 consumer index is taken. If the consumer index rose in November 2013 at a rate far below the normal average, a base effect raising the annual inflation in November 2014 will be observed.
Baz Puan: A unit of measurement expressing changes in interest rates. It corresponds to the fourth digit after the decimal point (0.0001). For example, if the interest rate rises from 5.25% to 6.75%, there is an increase of 150 basis points. In other words, a change of 100 basis points corresponds to a change of 1%.
Başabaş noktası: The point at which total revenue equals total cost, so that economic profit is zero.
Bedavacı sorunu: The situation in which some economic units use more than their share of a good or service, or do not pay the cost falling to their share.
Beklenen değer: Or in short EV: the operation of taking a probability-weighted average.
Beklenen eksik: The average loss incurred when the VaR threshold is exceeded; it measures tail risk better than VaR.
Beklenen fayda: Or in short EU: the operation of taking the probability-weighted average of utility.
Beklenti Yönetimi: Within the monetary policy framework, expectation management is the set of strategies the CBRT applies with the aim of ensuring that the medium- and long-term inflation expectations of economic units are shaped in line with the inflation targets.
Benchmarking: An undertaking's examination of the business techniques of other enterprises with high competitiveness, comparing them with its own techniques, and applying the information obtained from this comparison in its own business, with the aim of raising its competitive strength.
Beşeri sermaye: The human accumulations used in production, such as education, skill, experience and entrepreneurship.
Bid Rigging, Collusive Bidding: (Tendering) Cartels formed by undertakings to raise prices, share quantities or regions, or lower the quality of goods or services, vis-à-vis buyers seeking to procure products or services through a tendering process. Cartel members run the cartel through methods such as determining the order of winning, sharing the tenders among themselves, and artificially providing shares to the losers from the winner.
Big Data: Big data refers to large-volume data sets that cannot be analyzed by traditional information methods and require new solutions to be processed, that can generally be produced in large quantities within a short time, that are collected from different sources, and that can contain structured or unstructured data. With the valuable insights it provides, big data gives an undertaking the opportunity to better analyze consumer preferences and behaviors, thereby enabling innovative and high-quality
Bileşik Faiz: The interest applied to the total amount obtained after the interest amount accruing to an investor's principal held at the bank is added to the principal.
Bir Hafta Vadeli Repo Faiz Oranı: In May 2010, the CBRT introduced the one-week repo interest rate as a new liquidity instrument.
Bir hafta vadeli repo ihale faiz oranı: The interest rate applied for the transaction in which banks sell the securities they hold to the CBRT for one week and buy them back at maturity.
Bireysel arz: Or in short s: the quantity of a product that a single seller in the market wants to sell, depending on different prices, in a given period.
Bireysel talep: Or in short d: the quantity of a product that a single buyer in the market wants to purchase, depending on different prices, in a given period.
Birikmiş Faiz: The interest accumulated on an investment within the investment period, up to the payment date. For example, to purchase a government bond issued at 100 TL with a periodic 4% coupon payment every 6 months (182 days), the price to be paid 3 months later (91 days) is 102 TL, under the assumption that the market interest rate has not changed.
Birim esnek ilişki: A one percent increase in one variable resulting in a one percent response in the other variable.
Birim İşgücü Maliyeti: Refers to the average labor expenditures required to produce one unit of output. It is calculated by dividing total wage payments by production. It can also be expressed as the ratio of hourly wages to labor productivity. An increase in hourly wages raises unit labor cost, while an increase in productivity lowers it. From the firm's perspective, an increase in unit labor cost is a factor that reduces profitability and weakens competitiveness.
Birinci derece fiyat ayrımcılığı: Or perfect price discrimination: the practice of selling a given product to each buyer at the highest price that buyer is willing to pay for it.
Birinci fiyat kapalı teklif ihalesi: A type of auction in which participants submit sealed bids and the highest bidder wins and pays the price it bid.
Birincil Gelir Hesabı: Shows the incomes obtained in return for providing labor, financial or natural resources, and the amounts paid; it includes employees' wages as well as investment income and expenditure related to direct investments, portfolio investments and other investments.
Birleşme: The coming together of two firms of their own will to form a single new firm.
Birlikte arz edilen mallar: Each of the multiple products obtained as output at the end of the same production process.
Biyokütle: A renewable energy source defined as the mass that plant or animal organisms possess at a given time.
Block Exemption: Used to describe the regulations granting exemption to certain types of agreements as a group. In Turkish competition law, these regulations are made through block exemption communiqués. Agreements within the scope of a block exemption are exempt from the prohibitions on restrictive agreements, provided they satisfy the conditions relating to the block exemption. Such agreements are automatically valid and enforceable.
Bolluk çelişkisi: Or the resource curse: the phenomenon of natural resources such as oil bringing conflict, war, corruption and poverty instead of economic growth in some countries.
Bono: Securities with a maturity of less than one year, for which the issuing institution undertakes to pay a certain amount at the maturity it foresees. Issues with a maturity of less than one year made by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye trade under the name Treasury Bills (Hazine Bonosu). The English equivalent 'Bond' refers to instruments with maturities longer than 10 years (maximum 30 years) for US Treasury issues. Similarly, 'Note' is used for issues of 1-10 years, and 'Bill' for issues of one year or shorter.
Borç-özsermaye oranı: The ratio of total debt to equity; it shows the level of financial leverage. As the ratio rises, financial risk increases.
Boycott: Agreements not to do business with certain individuals or undertakings are called boycotts, and such behavior can be prohibited, particularly when the boycotting undertakings hold market power. Group boycotts of this kind may, for example, be used in pursuit of a price-fixing agreement. Accordingly, some rivals may decide not to do business with the others unless certain conditions are met, and this will bring about an increase in price levels. Not doing business with others
